statement: Let scores(items,d) be the list of all items[i][1] such that 0 <= i < len(items) and items[i][0] = d. Let top5sum(items,d) be the sum of the five largest elements of scores(items,d), counting multiplicities; equivalently, the maximum over all choices of five pairwise distinct indices i1,...,i5 with items[ik][0] = d of items[i1][1]+...+items[i5][1]. Let top5avg(items,d) = top5sum(items,d) / 5 using integer division (floor, since top5sum(items,d) >= 0). For every items satisfying the preconditions, whenever high_five(items) returns a result r, let ids be the list of distinct IDs occurring in items sorted in strictly increasing order. Then len(r) = len(ids), and for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), len(r[j]) = 2, r[j][0] = ids[j], and r[j][1] = top5avg(items, ids[j]).
preconditions: items is a slice of Vec<I64> with 1 <= len(items) <= 1000. For every i with 0 <= i < len(items), len(items[i]) = 2, 1 <= items[i][0] <= 1000, and 0 <= items[i][1] <= 100. For every distinct ID d that occurs as items[i][0] for some i, the number of indices i with items[i][0] = d is at least 5.

Additionally, items' is a permutation of the entries of items (same length and same multiset of two-element vectors).
